lesson_title: Circles, Fences and Two Downhill Slopes: Geometry, Statistics and Finance Essentials
hook_text: Same car. Same 15% loss per year. One formula leaves you R9 760,50 richer.
clip_script: Straight-line depreciation is simple interest in reverse: A equals P, times, one minus i n. A car of eighty thousand rand losing fifteen percent per year for four years: eighty thousand times, one minus nought comma six — thirty-two thousand rand. Reducing-balance depreciation is compound in reverse: A equals P, times, one minus i, to the power n. Same car, same rate: eighty thousand times nought comma eight five to the fourth — forty-one thousand seven hundred and sixty rand and fifty cents. Reducing balance keeps more value, because each year's fifteen percent bites a smaller amount. Same rate, nine thousand seven hundred and sixty rand fifty apart — the formula choice IS the question.
visual_style: Two identical cars roll down two slopes side by side — one a straight ramp losing equal chunks, one a bouncing curve losing shrinking chunks; rand counters tick down at different speeds until the gap flashes between them at the bottom.
mood: Split-screen suspense — identical setup, diverging fortunes, one word in the question deciding everything.
pacing: Parallel build on the two slopes, tick-tock of the counters, sharp reveal of the gap, crisp takeaway.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision lesson and let the wording pick the formula before the marker picks your marks.
